# RV power station and solar combos

No single combo fits every RV. The right one depends on whether you need to run a roof AC. The sources I found list power stations and mention panels as add-ons, so none gave a complete priced bundle. Panels are usually bought separately.

## Pick by how you camp

**Weekend trips with a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with two 200W SolarSaga panels**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output and weighs about 24 lb. Solar input tops out at 400W, so two 200W panels use all of it ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- It can't be expanded with extra batteries.

**Better solar and room to grow: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and up to 1,000W of solar input. It expands to 5kWh and weighs about 28 lb ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- For an RV, 1kWh is small unless you add an expansion battery.

**Multi-day boondocking with a 30A RV port: Bluetti AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output and 1,200W of solar input. It weighs about 62 lb ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). One source says it has a built-in 30A RV outlet ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- At 2,400W, it may not start a 13,500 BTU AC, which can spike past 3,000W.

**Running a roof AC or full-timing: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- The DELTA Pro 3 has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous output and expands past 12kWh. It is very heavy, a two-person lift ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- The Jackery 3000 Pro has 3,024Wh and 3,000W, with 6,000W surge, and is simpler to use ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, so ignore its Canadian electrical rules. The product specs still apply.

**Best capacity per dollar: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456Wh, 3,600W continuous output (6,000W peak), an RV outlet and 2,000W of solar input across three inputs. The warranty is 5 years.
- The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15) brings it to about $1,319. The site says it tested the code in the store's cart.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install. Reaching the full 2,000W of solar needs panels on all three inputs.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. [Product page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).

## Solar panel sizing
- A 300–400W folding array refills a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- Check the station's solar input limit first. A big array is wasted on a unit that caps at 400W.
- Panel options mentioned in the sources are the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase and Jackery SolarSaga 100W/200W ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).

## My suggestion
- **Roof AC or full-timing:** the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the strongest fit. The ALLPOWERS R4000 is the budget route.
- **Fridge, devices and Starlink:** the Jackery 1000 v2 with two 200W panels is simplest. The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus is better if you may expand later.

The review sites only offered "check price" buttons, with no direct retailer URLs I could pass on. Prices change often, so confirm current price and specs on the retailer's page. For the models above, start with the review pages linked in each section.

If you tell me your RV's AC size, fridge type and typical trip length, I can narrow this to one pick and a panel count.
